spec_features.spec_quote: an optional `give_up` sentinel (`<<GIVE_UP>>`) the model *may but need not* emit
spec_features.evidence: config.py:112 `give_up_sentinel: str = "<<GIVE_UP>>"`; harness.py:216 system prompt instructs the model it 'may emit the exact token {give_up} on its own line to stop'; harness.py:262-263 `if give_up_sentinel in assistant_text: stop_reason = "give_up"` and harness.py:282 `if stop_reason == "give_up": break`. The sentinel is delivered to the subject and detection actually breaks the turn loop.
spec_features.notes: Real end-to-end: instruction text delivered AND detection honored as a stop. The model may but need not emit it.

spec_features.spec_quote: voluntary termination is a first-class, analyzable signal
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:263 sets stop_reason="give_up"; TurnRecord.stop_reason (harness.py:54,66) is serialized into the persisted transcript via _append_transcript. So voluntary termination is recorded as a distinct, persisted, analyzable field.
spec_features.notes: Same underlying give_up mechanism; the stop_reason is stored in the transcript JSON so it is analyzable. Note: stop_reason is NOT written into scores.jsonl (run.py:_write_score omits it), but it is in the transcripts, so the signal is recorded.

spec_features.spec_quote: A turn loop bounded by the category's `turn_budget`
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:228 `budget = task.turn_budget`; harness.py:229 `for turn_index in range(budget)`; harness.py:264-265 `elif turn_index == budget - 1: stop_reason = "turn_budget"`. Loop is genuinely bounded by the per-category budget (builder.py:191/208/228/245/262 set turn_budget per category from config DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS). The loop terminates after `budget` turns.
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop bound; per-category budgets (e.g. extended=30) are passed through. This caps episode length but is a neutral loop bound, not framed as welfare.
